name: eBay
description: Largest general auction/fixed-price marketplace. 13.25% final value fee (most categories, includes payment processing) on item + shipping, capped at $750/item, plus $0.30 per order. 250 free listings/month, then $0.35 each. Store subscriptions reduce fees. Payout to bank, typically 1–3 business days.

quickFacts.label: Store plans
quickFacts.value: Basic/Premium/Anchor — lower FVF + more free listings

quickFacts.label: Best for
quickFacts.value: Anything — widest buyer reach, auctions for collectibles

pros: Largest buyer reach of any marketplace — highest sale prices for most categories
Auctions create urgency and price discovery for collectibles
Managed payments include processing — no separate Stripe/PayPal fee
250 free listings/month keeps entry cost zero
cons: 13.25% FVF + $0.30/order is higher than specialist resale apps
Seller performance standards are strict — defects can restrict account
Managed payments hold funds for new sellers initially
Buyer-friendly returns/policies can favour buyers in disputes
reviewData.reviewBody:
eBay remains the largest general marketplace: 13.25% final value fee on item+shipping (most categories, capped at $750/item) plus $0.30 per order, with payment processing included, 250 free listings/month ($0.35 above), and bank payouts in 1–3 business days. Store subscriptions reduce the FVF and add free listings. Auctions drive price discovery for collectibles, sneakers and rare goods.

The fee is higher than specialist resale apps (Vinted 0%, Mercari 10%), but eBay's buyer reach usually nets higher sale prices. New sellers face initial funds holds, and seller-performance standards are strict. For volume sellers, a Store subscription pays for itself quickly.
reviewData.testNotes: 13.25% FVF + $0.30/order + 250 free listings verified 25 Sep 2026 against eBay and multiple 2026 fee comparisons. Category-specific rates vary (books/DVDs/music higher). No live account test performed.

name: Vinted
description: Secondhand fashion marketplace (EU, UK, US). Sellers pay 0% commission and no listing fee — buyers pay a Buyer Protection fee (~5% + ~£0.70/€0.70). Payout to bank/PayPal after buyer confirms. (Source listed Vinted and Vinted UK separately — merged into one entry.)

quickFacts.value: Prepaid label, buyer pays; drop-off within 5 days

quickFacts.label: Payout
quickFacts.value: Bank or PayPal, released after buyer confirms

pros: 0% seller fee — you keep 100% of your listed price
Huge secondhand-fashion buyer base across EU/UK/US
No listing fees — free to list unlimited
Buyer Protection builds trust and reduces fraud
cons: Buyer fee raises effective price for buyers — can reduce offers
Payout held until buyer confirms (can be delayed)
Anti-automation stance bans cross-listing tools
Strictly fashion/secondhand — not for general goods
reviewData.reviewBody:
Vinted is the 0%-seller-fee secondhand fashion marketplace across the EU, UK and US: sellers list free and keep 100% of their price, while buyers pay a Buyer Protection fee (~5% + ~£0.70) that funds escrow and dispute cover. Shipping is via prepaid label (buyer pays), and payout releases to bank or PayPal after the buyer confirms receipt.

It's the cheapest major resale channel for sellers, but the buyer-side fee raises effective prices, payout is held until confirmation, and Vinted's anti-automation stance restricts cross-listing tools. It dominates secondhand fashion; for general goods or collectibles, eBay/Mercari reach further. (The source file listed Vinted and Vinted UK as two entries — they are the same platform; merged.)
reviewData.testNotes: 0% seller fee and Buyer Protection (~5% + £0.70) verified 25 Sep 2026 against Vinted's official how-it-works pages (updated Sep 2026). Duplicate Vinted UK entry merged. No live account test performed.

name: Depop
description: Social marketplace for vintage, Y2K and streetwear (Gen-Z focus). 0% commission in US/UK (10% in AU/EU) plus payment processing 3.3% + $0.45. Boosted listings cost an extra ~8%. Payout via PayPal/Stripe. US, UK, AU, EU.

cons: 10% commission in AU/EU
Payment processing (3.3% + $0.45) on top
Boosted listings (the main way to reach buyers) add ~8%

reviewData.reviewBody:
Depop is the social, Gen-Z-focused marketplace for vintage, Y2K and streetwear. In the US/UK it charges 0% commission (10% in AU/EU) plus 3.3% + $0.45 payment processing; optional boosted listings (the primary way to reach non-followers) add ~8% on those sales. Payouts run via Depop Payments (Stripe) or PayPal.

It achieves the highest prices for vintage/Y2K/streetwear, and the follower model builds repeat customers, but the audience is narrow and boosted-listing costs can stack. For mainstream or non-fashion goods, eBay or Vinted reach more buyers.
reviewData.testNotes: 0% US/UK commission (10% AU/EU), 3.3%+$0.45 processing and ~8% boost fee verified 25 Sep 2026 against 2026 marketplace-fee comparisons. No live account test performed.

name: Etsy
description: Marketplace for handmade, vintage (20+ years) and craft supplies. $0.20 per listing (4-month renewal) + 6.5% transaction fee (item+shipping) + payment processing ~3% + $0.25. Offsite Ads 12–15% on attributed sales (mandatory for shops >$10k/yr). Payout to bank/PayPal, daily/weekly.

pros: Strong Google SEO — buyers find listings via search
Best buyer intent for handmade, vintage, craft supplies
Low $0.20 listing cost to test products
Etsy Payments handles processing and chargebacks
cons: Stacked fees ($0.20 + 6.5% + ~3%+$0.25 + Offsite Ads) = ~13–15% effective
Offsite Ads mandatory (12–15%) for shops over $10k/yr — can't opt out
Listing fee charged even if item never sells
Saturated categories — price competition is intense
reviewData.reviewBody:
Etsy is the handmade/vintage/craft-supplies marketplace with strong Google SEO. Fees stack: $0.20 per listing (renewed every 4 months, even if unsold), 6.5% transaction fee on item+shipping, ~3% + $0.25 payment processing, and Offsite Ads at 12–15% on attributed sales (mandatory for shops doing over $10k/year). Combined effective rate is typically ~13–15%, higher with Offsite Ads. Payouts run daily or weekly to bank/PayPal.

Etsy Plus ($10/mo) adds listing/ad credits but no fee discount. The SEO buyer intent is unmatched for handmade/vintage, but saturated categories and mandatory Offsite Ads at scale erode margins. Many sellers use Etsy as a discovery channel and move repeat buyers to their own Shopify store.
reviewData.testNotes: Fee stack ($0.20 listing, 6.5% transaction, 3%+$0.25 processing, 12–15% Offsite Ads) verified 25 Sep 2026 against Etsy's legal fees policy (Feb 2026) and 2026 fee guides. No live account test performed.

name: Gumroad
description: Sell digital products, memberships and physical goods — no monthly fee, 10% platform fee + payment processing (Stripe/PayPal). Simple setup, audience tools built in. Payout weekly via Stripe/PayPal.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Gumroad is the no-monthly-fee platform for digital products, memberships and physical goods: 10% platform fee on every sale plus Stripe/PayPal processing (~2.9% + $0.30), with hosted product pages, built-in followers/email tools, and weekly payouts. It's the fastest way to start selling with zero setup cost.

The 10% fee is higher than Payhip's 5% (free plan) or a Shopify store (subscription but 0% platform fee), and you must drive your own traffic — Gumroad has no marketplace buyer pool. Best for creators with an existing audience testing a product; at scale, moving to Payhip Pro ($29/mo, 0%) or Shopify saves the 10%.
reviewData.testNotes: 10% fee, no monthly fee and weekly payout verified 25 Sep 2026 against Gumroad's pricing and 2026 creator-platform comparisons. No live account test performed.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Mercari is the low-maintenance general resale app (US; Japan is a separate platform): flat 10% seller fee, and since January 2025 the seller payment-processing fee is eliminated (buyers pay a 3.6% protection fee instead). Listings and relists are free; standard ACH payout is free, with a $2 Instant Pay option for fast cash.

It's simpler than eBay's fee stack and lower-maintenance than Poshmark's sharing model, but sale prices for collectibles are lower than eBay and it's US-only. For low-to-mid price general goods with minimal effort, it's a solid secondary channel alongside eBay and Vinted.
reviewData.testNotes: 10% flat fee, Jan 2025 processing-fee elimination and 3.6% buyer protection fee verified 25 Sep 2026 against 2026 resale-fee comparisons. No live account test performed.

name: Poshmark
description: Social fashion resale (US/CA; exited AU/UK/India in 2023). Flat $2.95 fee on sales under $15; 20% commission on sales $15+. Includes prepaid shipping label (up to 5 lb). No listing or payment-processing fees. Payout via direct deposit or check.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Poshmark is the social fashion/beauty/home resale app (US/CA only — exited AU/UK/India in Nov 2023). Fees are all-inclusive: flat $2.95 on sales under $15, 20% on sales $15+, and that includes a prepaid USPS Priority Mail label (up to 5 lb) and payment processing — no separate listing or processing fees. Payouts via direct deposit or check.

The 20% commission is high versus Vinted (0%) or Depop (0% US/UK), and US/CA-only limits reach. Active sellers who share listings and join 'parties' get the most visibility. For fashion/beauty in the US, it's a proven channel; elsewhere, Vinted/Depop/eBay dominate.
reviewData.testNotes: $2.95 under $15 / 20% $15+ all-in fee and US/CA-only status verified 25 Sep 2026 against Poshmark's fee pages and 2026 comparisons. No live account test performed.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Facebook Marketplace is the local classifieds layer on Facebook: 0% fee for local pickup (cash or in-person payment), and 5% (min $0.40) for shipped sales with checkout. No listing fees, and reach is massive. It's the best channel for bulky items, furniture, vehicles and anything expensive to ship.

The trade-off is trust: local cash deals have no buyer/seller protection, and low-ball offers, no-shows and scams are common. For shipped goods, the 5% fee plus your own shipping costs often make eBay/Mercari cheaper. Treat as a local-first channel, with safe public meetups or porch pickup.
reviewData.testNotes: 0% local / 5% shipped (min $0.40) fee verified 25 Sep 2026 against Meta's selling policies and 2026 marketplace comparisons. No live account test performed.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Craigslist is the original local classifieds: free listings in most categories (some US paid categories like jobs/gigs/services cost $5 per listing), 0% sale fee, cash in person, no account required. It remains useful for local, bulky, low-value items, rentals and job postings where reach matters more than polish.

Trust is the lowest of any channel — scams and spam are endemic, there's no buyer/seller protection or payment infrastructure, and the interface is dated. Facebook Marketplace has largely overtaken it for consumer goods. Use for the categories it still dominates (rentals, jobs, free/cheap local stuff) and always meet in public.
reviewData.testNotes: Free listings + $5 paid US categories and 0% sale fee verified 25 Sep 2026 against Craigslist's help pages. No live account test performed.

OfferUp is the US local marketplace (it absorbed Letgo): free local listings with 0% fee for in-person cash sales, optional shipping (with a seller service fee, commonly cited ~12.9%), and optional paid promoted listings. It offers in-app messaging, buyer/seller ratings and TruYou verification — a trust layer above Craigslist.

It's US-only, and shipped-sale fees are high versus eBay/Mercari, so it works best as a local channel. Visibility in busy categories often requires paid promotion. For local general goods it's a solid Facebook Marketplace alternative; for shipped or collectible items, eBay/Mercari net more.
reviewData.testNotes: Free local model and ~12.9% shipped seller service fee verified 25 Sep 2026 against OfferUp's help pages and 2026 comparisons; exact shipped fee may vary — confirm in dashboard. No live account test performed.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Whatnot is the live-shopping (livestream auction) marketplace for collectibles — trading cards, sneakers, comics, coins, vintage and fashion. Sellers pay 8% on live sales plus ~2.9% + $0.30 payment processing, with fast bank payouts. The live auction format creates bidding urgency and often achieves higher prices than fixed listings.

A seller application is required, and the format demands real livestreaming effort (time, presentation, community building). It's not open self-service and is collectibles-niche. For dedicated collectors/sneaker resellers with a following, the 8% fee and auction upside beat eBay; for casual or general-goods sellers, the format is too much work.

Buyer reach is smaller than Facebook Marketplace or eBay UK, and visibility often requires paid promotion. Best as a supplementary local channel alongside Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree; not suited to high-volume shipping.

The trade-off is traffic: OnBuy's buyer base is a fraction of Amazon/eBay, and brand recognition is low. It's best as an additional sales channel for UK/EU sellers already on Amazon/eBay — the lower fee margin on incremental sales can be worth the listing effort. Not a primary channel on its own.

The joining fee and ~25% commission are the highest in the handmade category (vs Etsy's ~13–15% effective), but curation means less price competition and higher sale prices, plus the brand's marketing exposure. reviewData.reviewBody:
Shopify is the leading hosted e-commerce platform: $39/mo Basic (raised from $29 in 2024) up to $399/mo Advanced, plus Shopify Payments processing (~2.9% + $0.30 in the US). Using an external payment gateway adds a 0.5–2% transaction fee, so most sellers use Shopify Payments, which pays out to bank. You own your storefront, brand and customer data — no marketplace rules.

The cost is traffic: unlike a marketplace, you drive 100% of visitors, and app/theme costs stack. Best for serious DTC brands ready to invest in marketing; for casual or low-volume sellers, a marketplace (Etsy/eBay) or Big Cartel's free plan is cheaper to start. Many sellers use marketplaces for discovery and Shopify for repeat customers.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Payhip sells digital products, memberships, courses and physical goods: free plan charges 5% per transaction (half of Gumroad's 10%), and the $29/mo Pro plan removes the platform fee entirely. Payment processing (Stripe/PayPal) still applies and pays out directly. EU VAT handling is built in, a real plus for EU sellers.

No marketplace traffic — you bring your audience — and brand recognition is smaller than Gumroad. But on cost it's the best digital-product platform: 5% to start, 0% at $29/mo. For creators selling digital products/memberships at any volume, it beats Gumroad on margin.

Creators earn a revenue share commonly cited around 50–60% (exact varies by tier/partner — verify in dashboard), with no monthly fee and PayPal payouts. The platform cut (~40–50%) is high versus selling on your own Payhip/Gumroad store (5–10%), and categories are saturated with a high quality bar. Best as a discovery/passive-income channel alongside your own store; top creators often use Creative Market for reach and their own store for margin.

reviewData.reviewBody:
Redbubble is the print-on-demand marketplace: upload art, set your margin (typically ~20–30% of retail, i.e. a few dollars per sale) on top of the base production price, and Redbubble handles printing, shipping and customer service across 70+ products. Zero upfront cost, built-in marketplace traffic, payouts monthly via PayPal/bank. Redbubble introduced tiered artist fees (Standard/Premium) that can reduce low-volume sellers' earnings — verify current.

Margins are thin and the marketplace is saturated, so generic designs don't sell — a niche or strong style is required. Best as passive income alongside other POD (TeePublic) and your own store (Sellfy/Shopify + a POD app). Monthly payout is slower than weekly marketplaces.

The royalty is very low and volume depends on frequent sitewide sales, so earnings are modest unless you have many designs and a niche. Best used alongside Redbubble (same uploads can be cross-listed) as passive income; not a primary earner for most artists.

It's strongest in invitations/stationery and custom event merchandise (weddings, parties), where customization matters. Default royalty is low and traffic is weaker than Redbubble, but the adjustable royalty and custom-product niche make it a useful supplementary POD channel. reviewData.reviewBody:
StockX is the bid/ask ('stock market') marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, electronics and collectibles: sellers set an ask, buyers bid, and StockX authenticates every item before forwarding to the buyer. Seller fees are tiered by quarterly volume: 9% transaction (Level 1) down to 7.5% (Level 4), plus 3% payment processing — total ~10.5–12%. Payouts are fast after authentication via bank/PayPal.

The authentication service is the core value — it justifies premium prices for high-value items where fakes are common. The fee is significant, new sellers start at the top tier, and you ship to StockX first (extra step). For high-value sneakers/collectibles, the price premium usually outweighs the fee; for low-value items, eBay/Mercari net more.

reviewData.reviewBody:
GOAT is the sneaker/apparel marketplace (strong in used sneakers, where StockX focuses on deadstock), with authentication included. Seller commission is rating-based: 9.5% for top-rated sellers (≥90), rising to 15% (70–89) and 20% (50–69), plus a flat $5–$30 seller fee and a 2.9% cash-out fee (waived if you spend your balance on GOAT purchases). Payouts via ACH/PayPal.

For top-rated sellers the 9.5% rate is competitive, but low-rated sellers can pay 20%+fees — among the highest in resale. The rating system is slow to raise, and used-item condition disputes are common. Best for established sneaker sellers with a high rating; new sellers may net more on StockX (flat 9% start).

Vestiaire Collective is the pre-owned luxury fashion marketplace (EU/UK/US) with included authentication: sellers ship to an authentication center, then Vestiaire forwards to the buyer. Commission is tiered by sale price: 25% under $100, 20% ($100–499), 18% ($500–1,999), 15% ($2,000–4,999), 12% ($5,000+), plus ~3% payment processing. Payouts via bank/PayPal.

The authentication trust lets luxury items sell at premium prices, and high-value items ($5,000+) pay just 12%. But sub-$100 items pay 25% (better sold on Vinted/Depop), and the auth-center step adds time. Best for genuine mid-to-high-end luxury; for fast fashion, Vinted/Depop/eBay are cheaper and faster.

reviewData.reviewBody:
The RealReal is the US luxury consignment house: you drop off or get free in-home pickup (major cities), and they authenticate (in-house experts, the industry benchmark), price, photograph, sell and ship for you. Commission is tiered ~15–60% — high-value items pay the low end, low-value items the high end (fine jewelry/watches have a separate schedule). Payout via check/bank/PayPal after the sale clears.

It's the most hands-off option and achieves the highest prices for genuine high-end luxury, but the commission is the highest in resale (up to 60% on low-value items) and the cycle is slow (weeks to months). Best for high-value pieces you can't or don't want to sell yourself; for items under ~$500, Vestiaire or Vinted/Depop net more faster.

Grailed is the designer/streetwear/archive marketplace (women's Heroine merged into the main app in 2024). Seller commission is tiered: 9% on sales ≥$120, or 6% with a $1.99 minimum under $120, plus ~3.49% + $0.49 Stripe payment processing. Payouts via Stripe/PayPal. It consistently achieves the highest sale prices for designer, archive and streetwear because its buyer base is knowledgeable and willing to pay premium.

Sub-$120 items pay a relatively high effective rate, and the audience is niche — mainstream fashion sells poorly. For designer/streetwear/archive, it's the best net-price channel; for mainstream or fast fashion, Depop/Vinted/eBay reach more buyers at lower effective cost.

Rebag is the US luxury-handbag specialist: two seller options — Instant Access (outright purchase, instant quote, same-day payment) or consignment (lower fee, higher net, slower). Authentication is included, and payouts run via bank/PayPal. It covers Hermès, Chanel, Louis Vuitton and other luxury handbags.

The instant option is the fastest way to liquidate a luxury bag, but the outright price is well below resale value (Rebag needs margin). For maximum net, consignment with Rebag or listing yourself on Vestiaire Collective pays more, but takes weeks. Best when speed matters; otherwise compare quotes across Rebag, Vestiaire and The RealReal.
